content_html:
AliExpress is an online retail marketplace owned by Alibaba Group and launched in 2010 to let buyers outside China purchase directly from Chinese manufacturers, wholesalers and small businesses. It is a third-party marketplace: individual sellers list the products and handle fulfilment, while AliExpress provides the storefront, payment handling and a dispute process.

AliExpress and Alibaba.com are different services

The two sites share an owner but serve different customers. Alibaba.com is a business-to-business wholesale platform, typically for bulk orders with minimum quantities. AliExpress is business-to-consumer, so a single item can be bought at a time. Comparison guides from marketplace-software and seller-tool companies describe the same split. If you want one unit, AliExpress is the relevant site; if you are sourcing stock from a manufacturer, Alibaba.com is.

Who sells on it

Sellers are mostly small businesses in China, with some in other places such as Singapore. Because each store sets its own shipping method and processing time, two orders placed on the same day can arrive weeks apart. Listings usually show the seller's shipping options, estimated delivery window and store history before you pay.

Buyer Protection

AliExpress describes a Buyer Protection programme: if an item arrives significantly different from its description, is defective, or does not arrive within the protection period, the buyer can open a dispute to ask for a refund or replacement. Deadlines apply, so open a dispute from the order page before the protection period ends and keep photos of the item and packaging. The exact period and what counts as a valid claim are set in the current Buyer Protection terms.

Practical checks before you order

  • Look at how long the store has been open and how many orders its listing has completed.
  • Read the shipping line for your country, including the estimated delivery window and any customs charges.
  • Compare product photos with buyer photos in the item comments, which show the real item.
  • Pay inside the AliExpress checkout, never by an off-platform transfer a seller suggests, because Buyer Protection only applies to payments made through the site.

What we could not verify

We did not place an order or test a dispute, so we cannot say how quickly refunds are paid. Check the current Buyer Protection terms for the protection period and the claims process in your country.
